sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: A community radio ______ is required to operate a community radio station. These stations are expected to produce programmes in local ______.
Match: (i) Transmitter (ii) Studio with (a) from where a presenter makes announcements (b) through which we receive the radio broadcast on our sets.
Fill in the blanks: For radio, ______ and a ______ is required to receive the signals.
State true or false: (a) The Chief engineer heads the programme wing. (b) Engineers are responsible for the technical quality of broadcasts.
questions.answer: (a) False – the Station Director does. (b) True.

questions.q: Match: (i) Station Director (ii) Station Engineer (iii) Announcer (iv) AIR with (a) three-tier broadcasting (b) head of programme wing (c) head of engineering wing (d) presents programmes.
Expand: (i) LPT (ii) HPT (iii) FM (iv) MW.
questions.answer: (i) Low Power Transmitter. (ii) High Power Transmitter. (iii) Frequency Modulation. (iv) Medium Wave.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Discuss the role of the Station Engineer and Radio Announcer in a radio station.
questions.answer: The Station Engineer heads the engineering wing and is responsible for all technical work; the Radio Announcer presents the programmes and makes them interesting through voice.

questions.q: List any two functionaries of a radio station with their function.
questions.answer: Station Director: in charge of the station and programme wing. Programme producer: plans, produces and presents programmes.

questions.q: What is a sound lock?
questions.answer: An enclosed space with a heavy door before the studio that prevents unnecessary outside sounds from entering.

questions.q: Name the three tiers of AIR's broadcasting.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write a short note on community radio or private radio station.
questions.answer: Community radio serves a limited, homogenous community with developmental programmes in the local language and needs a licence (Anna FM); private radio stations such as Radio Mirchi are licensed commercial stations giving music and fun to the youth.

questions.q: Describe community radio and its operations. Give an example.
questions.answer: Community radio caters to the interests of a limited area; it needs a licence, produces local-language programmes stressing development though entertainment is allowed; example: Anna FM, India's first campus community radio.

questions.q: Explain the three-tier system of All India Radio.
questions.answer: National channel (since 18 May 1988; news, plays, music in Hindi, English and Urdu), regional stations (middle tier, including the North-eastern service at Shillong) and local radio (area specific).

questions.q: Describe the roles of the studio, control room and transmitter.
questions.answer: Studio: sound-proof room where programmes are produced; control room: technical area that sends the programmes to the transmitter; transmitter: sends waves to the listener's radio set.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the structure and functioning of a radio station.
questions.answer: Three wings: programme, engineering, administration. Studio (sound lock, woollen panels, announcer's booth) → control room → transmitter → listener. Functionaries: Station Director, Station Engineer, programme staff, transmission staff, announcers and artists.

questions.q: Describe the role played by different functionaries of a radio station.
questions.answer: Station Director, Station Engineer, technicians, programme executives, transmission executives, announcers and artists each handle planning, technical work, transmission and presentation.
